headline: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: The committee reviewed water and management budgets, including $176 million in water projects and $21 million for temporary housing, then deferred the item.
meeting.recap: The committee had one item: the proposed fiscal year 27 budget for Maui County.[[0:03:24]] About $21 million is set aside to support temporary housing in case federal funding is reduced.[[0:08:25]] The water director said the Board of Water Supply reviewed the water budget and approved it as is.[[0:14:20]] The water director said the top priority is developing new water sources for affordable housing.[[0:14:46]] Asked about using water reserves for $1.8 million in aquifer mapping, the director said it is still under discussion.[[0:58:01]] The water department's capital project budget totals $176 million, mostly from outside funding sources.[[1:09:21]] A council member spoke against proposed security screening, which an official compared to a metal detector.[[1:49:39]] Officials expect over $121 million in FEMA public assistance (disaster reimbursement), with about $77 million obligated so far.[[2:41:09]] About $96 million has been conditionally awarded for rebuilding the French Street Apartments.[[2:58:47]] The chair deferred the budget item, meaning it will be taken up later.[[3:38:33]]
meeting.next: The chair said the rest of the budget calendar depends on the storm and how active the emergency operations center is. The water department will answer a question about expected federal refunds in writing.

moments.q: "Our top priority is developing new water sources for affordable housing."
Debate over a metal detector at the county building

boards.name: Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

issues.oneLine: The water director described an essentially status quo operating budget.
issues.why: The director said new water sources matter most because that is how the county can get more housing.
issues.next: The department is discussing timing for aquifer mapping with county management.
issues.brief: The only new positions are 10 that would be filled only if the county acquires a water system.[[#1]] Watershed grants stay at the 4% level required by the county.[[#2]] About 20% of the water budget pays for energy.[[#3]]

issues.oneLine: Officials said much of the rebuild funding is going to 11 multifamily housing rebuilds.
issues.why: The managing director said heavy subsidies are needed to bring these projects back for people who already lived there.
issues.next: The managing director offered to follow up in writing with more details.
issues.brief: About $96 million has been conditionally awarded for the French Street Apartments rebuild.[[#1]] A council member raised concerns about county and federal funds being used to subsidize housing.[[#2]]

issues.oneLine: The budget includes about $21 million for temporary housing in case federal funding is reduced.
issues.why: The managing director said the $21 million plans for the worst case, if FEMA does not extend the housing mission.

deadlines.t: End of current federal approval for the housing mission.

issues.next: Officials expect a partial activation of the emergency operations center for the incoming storm.
issues.brief: Officials expect over $121 million in FEMA public assistance, with about $77 million obligated so far.[[#1]] The recovery grant program has filled 27 of its 56 positions.[[#2]] The managing director said a federal disaster declaration for the recent storms could take up to a few months.[[#3]]
